Definition: Percentage of the national population covered by at least one 4G/LTE mobile network signal, whether or not they subscribe to the service. 4G is the practical minimum for meaningful broadband connectivity enabling digital services.
revision_notes: Confirmed. ITU DataHub (2024) records 96% LTE/WiMAX population coverage for Sao Tome and Principe, consistent with CST's claim of over 90% coverage following its August 2023 commercial 4G launch (102 antennas across 34 locations) and Unitel STP's earlier 4G rollout. Score 5 (90%+) is supported by both originally cited sources and a fresh authoritative ITU figure.
revised_comments: Sao Tome and Principe has near-universal 4G/LTE population coverage. ITU DataHub records 96% population coverage by LTE/WiMAX signal in 2024, consistent with incumbent operator CST's reported coverage above 90% following its commercial 4G launch in August 2023 across 102 antennas in 34 locations, and with the earlier commercial 4G/LTE deployment by Unitel STP.

Definition: Whether the country has enacted legal or regulatory requirements mandating that certain categories of data (personal data, government data, financial data, or critical infrastructure data) be stored within national borders. Central to data sovereignty debates in Africa.
Value Name: Sectoral requirements only (e.g., financial or telecoms data)
Comments: Law 03/2016 restricts personal data transfers out-of-country (Articles 19/20) unless adequate protection; sectoral personal data law; score 3
revision_notes: Law 3/2016 is a general, cross-sectoral personal data protection law (Article 3 applies to any controller established in, or processing data via means located in, STP), not a sector-specific requirement as the original comment suggested; it is better characterised as a comprehensive requirement covering personal data as a broad category. Articles 19-20 condition transfer of personal data outside national territory on adequate protection existing in the destination country. Law 7/2017 established the National Data Protection Agency (ANPDP) with investigative and enforcement powers (including ordering the blocking, erasure or destruction of data, and authorising or restricting cross-border transfers), and ANPDP is demonstrably active (e.g. its 2025 collaboration with Facebook to remove fake profiles). No evidence was found of localisation requirements specifically for government, financial or critical-infrastructure data, so code 5 (multiple data types with enforcement) is not supported by current evidence; code 4 (comprehensive requirements for personal data/broad categories) better reflects the law than the originally recorded sectoral code 3.
revised_comments: Sao Tome and Principe has a comprehensive, cross-sectoral personal data protection framework rather than sector-specific data localisation rules. Law No. 3/2016 on the Protection of Personal Data applies broadly to any data controller established in, or processing personal data via means located in, the country, and Articles 19-20 restrict the transfer of personal data outside national territory unless the destination offers an adequate level of protection. The National Data Protection Agency (ANPDP), created under Law No. 7/2017, has investigative and enforcement powers, including the ability to order the blocking, erasure or destruction of data and to authorise or restrict cross-border transfers, and is actively engaged in enforcement activity, such as its 2025 collaboration with Facebook to remove fake profiles linked to public figures.

Definition: The number and activity level of technology hubs, incubators, accelerators, and co-working spaces focused on technology and innovation. These provide physical infrastructure and support for tech entrepreneurship and skills development.
revision_notes: The cited 2019 AfriLabs-Briter Bridges report (a survey of 100 hubs across Africa) does not list Sao Tome and Principe among featured countries, which is consistent with 'none identified' at that time. A general business incubator, REINA (Rede Nacional de Incubadoras e Aceleradoras de Negocios), has since opened (Incubadora Central, inaugurated March 2022, backed by the Ministry of Youth, Sports and Entrepreneurship and UNDP) and in 2025-26 joined UNDP's pan-African Timbuktoo incubator/accelerator network, which has some technology and innovation orientation. However, REINA's programming to date is predominantly general entrepreneurship (agribusiness, tourism, hospitality, gastronomy) rather than technology-specific, so it is unclear this meets the definition of a 'technology hub' as opposed to a general business incubator. Flagged for human review rather than asserting an upgrade to code 2 on this single, ambiguous source.
revised_comments: No hub, incubator or accelerator with a clear, dedicated focus on technology and innovation has been identified in Sao Tome and Principe. The country was not featured among the 100 hubs surveyed in the 2019 AfriLabs-Briter Bridges pan-African innovation ecosystem report. A general business incubator, REINA (Rede Nacional de Incubadoras e Aceleradoras de Negocios), operates a central facility in the capital, established in 2022 with Ministry of Youth and UNDP support, and joined the UNDP-backed pan-African Timbuktoo network in 2025-26; its activities to date, however, centre on general entrepreneurship across sectors such as agribusiness, tourism and hospitality rather than technology specifically.
